'''Sophie Morel''' (born 1979)<ref>Birth year from [http://d-nb.info/gnd/1146785763 German National Library catalog entry], retrieved 2021-03-24</ref> is a French [[mathematician]], specializing in [[number theory]]. She is a [[CNRS]] [[French National Centre for Scientific Research#Employment|directrice de recherches]] in mathematics at [[École normale supérieure de Lyon]]. In 2012 she received one of the ten prizes of the [[European Mathematical Society]].

== Biography ==
In a 2011 interview, Morel credited a math magazine bought while in 9th grade as well as summer camps for developing her interest in mathematics<ref>{{citation|title=An Interview with Sophie Morel, Part 1|pages=3–6|journal=Girls' Angle Bulletin|volume=5|issue=1|date=October 2011 |url=http://www.girlsangle.org/page/bulletin-archive/GABv05n01E.pdf}}</ref>  and in a 2012 interview she mentioned being a keen distance runner.<ref name="wim">{{citation|title=Interview: Sophie Morel, Harvard University |url=http://www.europeanwomeninmaths.org/women-in-math/portrait/sophie-morel|publisher=European Women in Mathematics|journal=EWM Newsletter|volume=21|date=November 6, 2012|pages=8–9}}</ref>
She studied in [[Paris]] at the [[École Normale Supérieure]].<ref name="ENS"/> In 2005 she finished her Ph.D. at the University of Paris-Sud, under the supervision of [[Gérard Laumon]].<ref name="wim"/><ref name="ENS"/> Her thesis made progress on the [[Langlands program]].<ref name="wim"/>

After her Ph.D., she was a [[Clay Mathematics Institute|Clay Research Fellow]] between 2005 and 2011. In December 2009 she was appointed as a professor of mathematics at [[Harvard University]],<ref>{{citation|url=http://news.harvard.edu/gazette/story/2010/01/mathematician-gains-dual-appointments/|title=Mathematician gains dual appointments Sophie Morel will join FAS, Radcliffe Institute|date=January 14, 2010|first=Steve|last=Bradt|newspaper=Harvard Gazette}}.</ref> becoming the first woman in mathematics to be [[tenure]]d there.<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2010/03/13/education/13harvard.html?_r=0|title=Women Making Gains on Faculty at Harvard|first=Tamar|last=Lewin|newspaper=[[The New York Times]]|date=March 12, 2010}}.</ref> From 2012 to 2020, she was a professor of mathematics in [[Princeton University]], where she was also the Henry Burchard Fine Professor in 2015.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.princeton.edu/news/2014/04/07/faculty-chosen-endowed-professorships |website=[[Princeton University]] |title=Faculty chosen for endowed professorships |author=Office of Communications |accessdate=March 21, 2021}}</ref> Morel moved to the École Normale supérieure de Lyon as a [[CNRS]] [[French National Centre for Scientific Research#Employment|directrice de recherches]] in mathematics in 2020.

==Recognition==
She gave an [[list of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers|invited talk at the International Congress of Mathematicians]] in 2010, in the "Number Theory" section.<ref>{{cite web|title=ICM Plenary and Invited Speakers since 1897|url=http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByCongress.php|publisher=[[International Congress of Mathematicians]]}}</ref>
In 2012 she received one of the prestigious [[European Mathematical Society]] Prize for young researchers, and in May 2013 she was announced as the winner of the inaugural 2014 [[AWM-Microsoft Research Prize in Algebra and Number Theory]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Prof. Sophie Morel wins inaugural AWM-Microsoft Research Prize in Algebra and Number Theory |url=http://www.math.princeton.edu/news/home-page/prof-sophie-morel-wins-inaugural-awm-microsoft-research-prize-algebra-and-number|publisher=Princeton University Mathematics Department}}</ref><ref name="ENS">{{cite web |url=https://www.ens.psl.eu/portraits-de-normaliens/sophie-morel |website=[[École normale supérieure (Paris)|École normale supérieure]] |title=Sophie Morel |language=fr |accessdate=March 21, 2021}}</ref>
